sections.label: Wakaf asset governance and audit
sections.summary: Wakaf assets are managed by Warees Investments, MUIS subsidiary and mutawallis, with governance, audit requirements under AMLA and periodic MUIS checks.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The wakaf assets are managed by Warees Investments, a subsidiary of MUIS, and the appointed mutawallis, in accordance with the intentions of the wakif or donor.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: There are clear governance mechanisms in place to ensure that wakaf assets remain financially sustainable and are managed with accountability and transparency.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Second, Warees and the appointed mutawallis must comply with audit requirements set out under the AMLA, as well as undergo periodic checks by MUIS that religious guidance by the Fatwa Committee has been adhered to.

sections.label: Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme initiatives
sections.summary: MUIS and Warees have undertaken asset enhancement and redevelopment initiatives under the Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme for some wakaf properties.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For some wakaf properties, MUIS and Warees have also undertaken asset enhancement and redevelopment initiatives under the Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme to optimise financial returns while sustaining their heritage value.

sections.label: Wakaf returns distributed to beneficiaries
sections.summary: Returns from building rentals and other wakaf income are distributed per the wakaf deed, with $11.3 million disbursed in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, the returns from the building rentals, as with any other forms of income generated from the wakaf assets are distributed to beneficiaries in accordance with the wakaf deed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2024, a total of $11.3 million was disbursed to the wakaf beneficiaries, which include the family members of the benefactors, as well as mosques, madrasah, community organisations and charities.

sections.label: Jamae Chulia restoration and future
sections.summary: Jamae Chulia Mosque restoration is completed, Jamae Chulia Heritage will be completed soon, and wakif intentions are held with trust.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As the Member can see, the Jamae Chulia Mosque restoration has been completed and the Jamae Chulia Heritage is going to be completed soon.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And not only do we want to develop for today, I think the key, what I got from my engagement, is that the community leaders want to do this for the future generation as well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, I assure the Member that we will do our best to ensure that what the wakif would like to leave behind is not only acceded to, but we hold it with trust.
